app.failed: The building lost power. Reload to try again.
app.narrow: 3 AM is built for a desktop screen, 900 px or wider. In a narrower window the monitor does not fit: open it on a computer or widen the window.
window.label: The window: the city, and the evidence taped to the glass
sill.caption: {title} · Mercadito · {clock}
tour.clock.title: The clock moves only when you act
tour.clock.body: This is a simulated on-call shift. Reading, thinking and moving around the screen cost nothing. Every query, mitigation or message costs case minutes, and the cost is on its button before you use it.
tour.phone.title: The phone wakes you
tour.phone.body: The page lands here: press “{ack}” to start. The phone keeps the time, an estimate of affected users and questions from people who need to know what is going on. Replying costs minutes too.
tour.monitor.title: The monitor holds your tools
tour.monitor.body: Tabs: {tabs}. Metrics speaks PromQL; logs and traces take short filters explained under each box. If you type something the desk does not understand, it says so and charges nothing.
tour.receipts.title: Every query prints a receipt
tour.receipts.body: Receipts stack between the monitor and the phone. Click one to see its result again without paying twice.
tour.evidence.title: Tape evidence to the window
tour.evidence.body: Tear off what matters with “{tear}”: a log line, a change, a span. On a chart, drag across the range. The slip sticks to the glass. The city behind it is the service map: a building turns red when its requests fail or crawl.
tour.hypotheses.title: Tie evidence to a hypothesis
tour.hypotheses.body: “{newHypothesis}” lets you write what you think is happening. Select a slip and click the hypothesis, or use “{tieHere}”. Mark it “{holds}” or “{alibi}” when the evidence decides; nobody grades it for you while you play.
tour.close.title: Act, then write it down
tour.close.body: Mitigations live in “{actions}”. After you apply one you watch the chart for a few minutes. Once the alert has been quiet for five minutes, “{close}” on the phone opens the postmortem, and then you see what was really going on. This tour comes back with “{tour}”, in the bar under the window.
reset.question: Clear every case, note and preference? The night starts over and nothing comes back.
folder.kicker: INCIDENT RESPONSE SIMULATION · MERCADITO, NIGHT SHIFT
folder.how: Every query costs minutes, and the clock only moves when you do something. Tear off what matters and tape it to the window. Tie it to a hypothesis. When you know enough, act. When it's quiet, write it down for the people who weren't there.
folder.honor: One rule: no outside help until the case is closed. The review comes after.
folder.closedBefore.one: You closed this case once. Same city, same bug; a different night of noise if you replay it.
folder.closedBefore.other: You closed this case {runs} times. Same city, same bug; a different night of noise if you replay it.
phone.label: Phone
phone.resolvedBody: The alert has been quiet for five minutes. The night isn't over until it's written down.
phone.holding: None new in the last minute.
phone.sunUp: The sun is up. The case is still open.
phone.statusPlaceholder: What's broken, who it hurts, what you're doing, when you'll say more.
monitor.label: Monitor
monitor.locked: Screen locked. The phone is the only thing awake.
metrics.subset: This desk speaks a subset of PromQL: selectors, rate, increase, histogram_quantile, sum/avg/min/max/count by, arithmetic and comparisons.
metrics.dragToPin: drag across the chart to tear off a range
metrics.noSeries: No series. Either nothing happened, or that isn't the question.
dashboard.hint: A dashboard is somebody else's guess about what matters. Usually a decent one.
logs.syntax: service:name  level:warn+  "text"  -exclude  trace:id  since:30m  from:03:00 to:03:20
logs.none: Nothing matched. Silence is also data, but not much.
changes.hint: Deploys, config pushes and flags since midnight.
actions.hint: Each action changes the system from the moment it lands. Some help. Some only feel like help.
watch.cleared: The line bends back. Quiet since {clock}.
watch.nothing: The alert did not quiet down. You watched for {minutes} minutes.
tray.label: RECEIPTS
tray.empty: Every query prints a receipt here. None yet.
board.empty: No evidence pinned. Start with what changed.
board.tieHint: Click a hypothesis, or use “tie here”, to tie this slip to it.
board.hypothesisPlaceholder: What do you think is going on?
error.promql.unsupported_function: This desk doesn't know that function.
error.promql.unsupported_aggregation: This desk doesn't do that aggregation.
error.promql.unsupported_feature: Real PromQL, but outside this desk's subset. Nobody's going to fake an answer.
error.promql.expected_range: That function wants a range, like [5m].
error.promql.expected_instant: A range vector can't go there. Wrap it in rate() or increase().
error.promql.expected_scalar: That argument has to be a plain number.
error.promql.scalar_comparison: Comparing two numbers needs the bool modifier, which this desk doesn't speak.
error.promql.empty_query: An empty query costs nothing and tells you the same.
error.filter.bad_value: That value doesn't fit the key.
error.filter.negated_key: A minus only excludes words; a filter key can't be negated.
rubric.status.impact: Includes at least one number (how bad it is).
rubric.status.nextUpdate: Includes a time or a delay (when you will write again).
rubric.status.length: Short enough to read on a phone ({length} characters).
rubric.status.namesPerson: You mention {name}. Does it explain a condition, or point at someone?
rubric.pm.timeline.fail: The timeline has {count} timestamped entries. It needs at least three.
rubric.pm.impact.pass: Impact includes at least one number.
rubric.pm.impact.fail: Impact has no numbers. "Some users" helps nobody plan.
rubric.pm.noDistractors.pass: No red herrings in the factor list.
rubric.pm.noDistractors.fail: At least one factor in the list had nothing to do with it.
rubric.pm.morethanOne.pass: More than one factor. Incidents rarely have just one.
rubric.pm.morethanOne.fail: Only one factor. Things that break at 3 AM usually needed help.
rubric.pm.blameless.fail: "{term}" points at a person. Nobody is to blame. Something made the mistake easy.
rubric.pm.actionsTyped.pass: Every action item has a type and an owner.
rubric.pm.actionsTyped.fail: Action items need at least two entries, each with a type and an owning team.
rubric.pm.actionsPrevent.pass: At least one action is marked prevent or process. Whether it really stops a repeat is your call.
rubric.pm.actionsPrevent.fail: No action prevents a repeat. Detection alone means you'll be paged faster next time.
rubric.pm.wentWell.pass: You wrote down what went well. That's what you'll want to keep.
rubric.pm.wentWell.fail: What went well is empty. Something did, or you wouldn't be writing this.
rubric.pm.selfReadable: Someone who slept through it could follow this.
rubric.pm.selfWhyNotWho: Every factor explains why it was possible, not who did it.
rubric.pm.namesPerson: You mention {name}. The sentence explains why that step seemed reasonable, not who got it wrong.
pm.title: {title}: what happened
pm.lede: Written for the morning shift. Facts first, no villains.
pm.timelineHint: One line per event, starting with the time (HH:MM).
pm.tl.stable: The alert has been quiet for five minutes.
pm.impactFacts: From the page to stable: {minutes} min. Users affected (estimated from failed or slow requests, not unique people): {users}.
pm.factorsHint: Pick every card that helped this happen. There isn't one root cause; there are conditions that lined up.
pm.customFactor: Another factor, in your own words (optional)
pm.reviewLede: A fixed rubric checks the shape: times, numbers, cards, action types and blame words. It cannot tell whether what you wrote is true or clear; you decide that in the questions below. Filing it closes the exercise; it certifies nothing.
debrief.title: What was really going on
debrief.contributing: In this case, removing any one of these would have kept the night quiet. That is why the postmortem asks for factors, not a culprit: a single "root cause" picks one box in the chain and hides the others, usually the ones nobody owns.
debrief.restartFirst: You restarted before you looked. Requests dropped for a minute, then everything went back to how it was: the restart never touched what was wrong. The telemetry survived here; in other systems a restart also takes the in-memory state you'd have wanted to see.
debrief.distractors.one: One red herring made it into your postmortem.
debrief.distractors.other: {count} red herrings made it into your postmortem.
debrief.missed.one: One contributing factor didn't make the list.
debrief.missed.other: {count} contributing factors didn't make the list.
